title:
A 🧵: The guys who are advocating for best of 3 at Slams are having a framing problem. (And it does appear to be a subset of men, which given what we know about biology and concrete thinking makes sense) 
But if I could get you guys to step back and view this a bit differently 🧠
author: Amy Lundy

title:
Big conclusion: 🥁 
It’s math. If you shorten the total available time that fans can engage with the sport— and that’s what would happen if you clip it to best of 3– you’re shooting yourself in the foot big time 
🦶💥🔫
author: Amy Lundy

title:
A best-of-5 match at a Grand Slam? Most fans aren’t going to see all of it. 
* That’s ok. Embrace it *
They’ll catch some of set 2, they’ll see a crucial break in set 4, they’ll go on their phone to see the crazy circus point they missed. Embrace the dipping in & out👇
author: Amy Lundy

title: Some journalists (sorry, particularly older ones) have trouble understanding this multi screen situation because the way they (we) tend to view a match is “locked in.” That’s the job— to tell the story.
author: Amy Lundy

title:
Therefore some people automatically think: Shorter attention span, shorten the sport.
But it’s actually counterintuitive.
It’s important to understand the difference between short attention and divided attention.
author: Amy Lundy
